html:
Ram Mohan Roy was a Bengali thinker and reformer, born in 1772, often called the father of the Bengal Renaissance and of modern India.

He was a brilliant linguist who read Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and English, and he studied Islam, Christianity and the Upanishads. He came to believe in one formless God and saw idol worship and much of priestly ritual as later corruptions.

His causes:

  • He campaigned hard against sati, the burning of widows, and backed the governor general when it was banned in Bengal in 1829.
  • He pressed for women's rights to property and against child marriage.
  • He argued for teaching science and English rather than only classical learning, and ran newspapers in Bengali and Persian.
  • In 1828 he founded the Brahmo Sabha, later the Brahmo Samaj, with Dwarkanath Tagore.

The Mughal emperor gave him the title Raja and sent him to Britain in 1830 to argue for a larger pension. He died at Bristol in 1833 and is buried there. His work shaped later reformers from Tagore's family to the Congress.
sum: Ram Mohan Roy was a Bengali thinker and reformer, born in 1772, often called the father of the Bengal Renaissance and of modern India.
